web_evidence.title: Excerpt from Atonement by Ian McEwan
web_evidence.note: Publisher-permitted Chapter One excerpt sustains third-person narration of Briony, corroborating the sampled third-person passages but proving only the opening.

web_evidence.title: ‘Your duplicitous point of view’: Delayed revelations of hypothetical focalisation in Ian McEwan’s Atonement and Sweet Tooth
web_evidence.note: Scholarly structural analysis describes Atonement as ostensibly heterodiegetic and states that Part Four switches to autodiegetic narration, with the ending giving first-person access to aged Briony.

web_evidence.title: Experience on Trial
web_evidence.note: University of Glasgow doctoral research explicitly identifies the earlier omniscient realist narration and the short final 'London, 1999' epilogue narrated by Briony in first person.

web_evidence.title: Text overview – Atonement
web_evidence.note: AQA's educational overview says the novel is, for the most part, conventionally third-person omniscient and explains that Briony writes about herself in third person.

web_evidence.title: Atonement: a novel
web_evidence.note: A searchable copy places q00707 within Briony's sustained first-person 'London, 1999' section; uncertain authorization limits this source to contextual corroboration.

person_note: Parts One through Three constitute the sustained base narrative and use third-person narration with free-indirect focalization. The comparatively short final 'London, 1999' coda is first person, but a terminal framing exception does not override the person controlling the main novel. Letters, dialogue, and local first-person material likewise remain subordinate, so the base label is THIRD.
